artifact: Verdi (Coq-verified Raft implementation, https://github.com/uwplse/verdi-raft) as analyzed in Fonseca et al., 'An Empirical Study on the Correctness of Formally Verified Distributed Systems', EuroSys 2017, https://www.cs.purdue.edu/homes/pfonseca//papers/eurosys2017-dsbugs.pdf (also covers IronFleet and Chapar)
property: Linearizability (safety) of the replicated key-value store built on verified Raft.
model: Verdi's network/failure semantics in Coq; the verified protocol handlers, extracted to OCaml and linked against an unverified OCaml shim.
trusted_base: unverified OCaml shim layer (networking, disk persistence, snapshots)
assumptions: recv returns a complete client request
disk writes and the snapshot/log sequence are atomic under crash
deployed: The Verdi key-value server running the extracted code with its shim over real TCP and a real disk, under crash and network fault injection.
gap: Of 16 bugs found across three verified systems, none was in the verified protocol code; Verdi's bugs were in the unverified shim, e.g. assuming recv returns a whole request and a snapshot/truncate order that loses data on crash, i.e. mismatches between the shim and the verified code's assumptions.

sources.title: An Empirical Study on the Correctness of Formally Verified Distributed Systems (EuroSys 2017)
sources.quote: Our results revealed that these assumptions referred to a small fraction of the trusted computing base, mostly at the interface of verified and unverified components.

sources.title: An Empirical Study on the Correctness of Formally Verified Distributed Systems (EuroSys 2017)
sources.quote: The Verdi server used TCP to receive client requests but wrongly assumed that the recv system call would return the entire request in a single invocation.

sources.title: An Empirical Study on the Correctness of Formally Verified Distributed Systems (EuroSys 2017)
sources.quote: Finding 5: No protocol bugs were found in the verified systems.
